cases.purpose: Flag text of every capability combination, including the word none: all 16 subsets of the four capability bits (flags 0x0-0xf, the empty subset prints none), the same with GENL_UNS_ADMIN_PERM (0x10-0x1f; the candidate has no word for that bit, so 0x10 alone prints none) and unknown or high bits (0x20 ... 0xffffff00, 0x80000000, 0xffffffff).
cases.oracle: Independent protocol oracle and mock: the helper runs the UNCHANGED candidate under a seccomp user-notification filter (no privilege) and answers its NETLINK_GENERIC socket(), bind() and sendmsg() itself: socket() is answered by injecting one end of an AF_UNIX SOCK_SEQPACKET socketpair at descriptor 100 (SECCOMP_IOCTL_NOTIF_ADDFD), the request is read out of the owned single-threaded child, and the reply datagrams are exactly the planned receive buffers; select, recvmsg and close then run natively. Table, capability flags and buffer boundaries are therefore exactly the synthetic plan, independent of the guest kernel. Replies are encoded by the helper's kernel-faithful encoder (byte-identical to all ten real records of the genl-review-100 guest and re-verified in setup against the live guest kernel), decoded again by the frozen oracle parser (genl-review-observer.py, digest-checked), and the expected text is the documented loadables/genl.c print contract rendered by the frozen oracle from the synthetic table, never taken from candidate output. Every request the candidate sends is decoded from its memory and asserted. Setup controls (a failure is an ERROR, never a candidate result): frozen known-answer tests; encoder round trip of every table; a Python probe making the candidate's syscalls receives the planned datagram bytes and boundaries at the injected descriptor and the request decoded from memory equals the request sent; other netlink protocols are not injected; and the real guest family table served through the mock reaches a client unchanged. The real controller never reports an operation without a flag word (0 of 138 operations on the genl-review-100 guest), so the none branch can only be exercised with a mock controller.
cases.comparison: commands=yes: #index and ID-0x.. of every operation; caps-hex=yes: Capabilities (0x..) equals the planned flags; word-admin/doit/dumpit/haspol=yes: each phrase appears for exactly the operations whose flags contain the bit; words-exact=yes: the whole flag line equals the source-contract text for every operation; none-words=yes: the word none appears for exactly the operations with none of the four bits, and there is at least one; injected=yes; request-dump=yes (the candidate request is a CTRL_CMD_GETFAMILY dump); status 0, empty stderr. Every key is evaluated for every vector (no early exit). Retained in the case tree: mock-observations.jsonl (candidate raw stdout, stderr, status, the expected bytes and datagram accounting per vector), mock-events-*.json (every intercepted call, the decoded request, datagram digests), the real-kernel transcripts of the setup controls, and the setup report as the stdout of the setup step.

cases.comparison: Each key is yes only if its control holds: base-known-answers: the frozen oracle known-answer tests pass; encoder-roundtrip: every synthetic table, encoded by the mock, decodes with the frozen parser to exactly the table; injection: a probe making the candidate syscalls got the injected socket at descriptor 100, bind answered, sendmsg returned the request length; boundaries: the probe received exactly the planned datagrams, with their boundaries and bytes, and a complete multipart conversation; decode-request: the request decoded from the probe memory equals the request the probe sent, and the decoded families equal the table; narrow: a NETLINK_ROUTE socket and an AF_UNIX socket are not injected and cause no notification; kernel-end-to-end: the real guest family table served through the mock reaches the probe unchanged; kernel-records: the mock encoding of every real guest record is byte-identical to the kernel record; kernel-like-errors: plain GETFAMILY and unknown name are refused with the real kernel errno; a known name and id return the family; no-strays: no child process remains after the supervised runs. Every key is evaluated for every vector (no early exit).
